summary: The Master Key invocation mismatch is caused by the JavaScript artifact.c invoke_untrap() wrapper returning without calling trap.c untrap(). C asks for a direction; the JavaScript replay leaves the invoke prompt on screen and consumes the next key as a game command. Port and wire invoke_untrap() to the existing untrap() implementation.

source.branch: When arti_invoke() selects an artifact whose invocation property is UNTRAP and its cost check succeeds, invoke_untrap() calls untrap(TRUE, 0, 0, NULL). That path asks for a direction. In this recording, the westward answer finds no known trap, so untrap() returns false and invoke_untrap() resets the artifact age and returns ECMD_CANCEL.
callers: artifact.c:arti_invoke() dispatches the UNTRAP case (2158); artifact.c:doinvoke() enters arti_invoke() (1749-1758).
dependencies: trap.c:untrap() (5848 onward), already implemented in js/trap.js:untrap(); its usual interactive path calls cmd.c:getdir() (3962-4019), already implemented in js/cmd.js:getdir().

evidence: challenges/evaluations/baseline-9f590c88f193a980f8f819ebfad051a65f36faa0-v29.json records the first mismatch at screen 70, step 70, key g (C cell I, JavaScript cell W), with the first RNG divergence at step 73. The recorded session challenges/cases/v29/v29-key-invoke-untrap.session.json shows that step 70 asks for an invocation direction in C; key h at step 71 then produces “You know of no traps there.”

nethack-c/upstream/src/artifact.c:1838-1846 implements invoke_untrap(): call untrap(TRUE, 0, 0, NULL); if it returns false, clear obj->age and return ECMD_CANCEL; otherwise return ECMD_TIME. artifact.c:2158 dispatches UNTRAP from arti_invoke().

nethack-c/upstream/src/trap.c:5848 onward shows that the usual untrap path calls getdir() before checking the target and returns false when no known trap or door is at that location. nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:3988 supplies the default “In what direction?” prompt.

At examined commit 9f590c88f193a980f8f819ebfad051a65f36faa0, js/artifacts.js:2410-2414 instead calls note_unported("trap.c untrap"), resets obj.age, and returns ECMD_CANCEL without calling untrap(). The existing js/trap.js:2823 untrap() and js/cmd.js:getdir() implementations are therefore bypassed. This leaves the invoke prompt on screen and lets the recorded h answer fall through as a normal command, matching the queue’s subsequent step-73 RNG divergence.

Implementation scope: port the whole artifact.c invoke_untrap() function and wire it to the existing JavaScript trap.untrap() function. Keep the C cancellation behavior when untrap() returns false. The source trace does not require a new trap.c port for this prompt/no-trap branch.
